name: VisualDx API
description:
The VisualDx API is a subscription-based service exposing programmatic access to VisualDx processes, text, and images.

#### All endpoints in the VisualDx API require authentication

Once you have received your **API Key** and **API Secret**, you may begin accessing the API by following the guide in *Getting Started*.

# Getting Started

This quick tutorial will provide you and overview of the VisualDx API and outline the steps to get started.

## Setup

The VisualDx API is a standard RESTful web service that accepts `GET` and `POST` requests.  The current version of the API is available using the base path `https://api.visualdx.com/v1/`. We recommend you build your integrations using a base-path that includes the API version path component.

## Authentication

The VisualDx API uses a standard Bearer HTTP Authorization header to authenticate your requests. You can use the `/auth/token` endpoint to exchange your credentials for a token.

> If you would like to request API credentials, please [contact us for a "Sales/Demo Inquiry"](https://www.visualdx.com/contact/) to set up an API account during our early-access phases.

The `access_token` provided by the token endpoint is valid for 24 hours, and you may authenticate as many active sessions as you like.

<SecurityDefinitions />

## Text Content

The VisualDx API returns formatted text content in one of the following formats:

### HTML

Text is returned as an HTML fragment using a safe subset of HTML tags:

- `i`
- `b`
- `br`
- `a`
- `sup`
- `sub`
- `ul`
- `ol`
- `li`

## VisualDx URI

The VisualDx API uses a custom URI format to link and locate additional API resources.  References take the following form:

### Diagnoses

      vdx://dx/<id>
- **id** (number) - the ID of the diagnosis


### External Codes

      vdx://code/<system>/<value>
- **system** (string) - the system for the code
- **code** (string) - the code value for the given system

## Audience

Most endpoints in the VisualDx API support multiple datasets:

* The **Clinical** dataset exposes all supported _Findings_ and _Conditions_, and content which has been tailored to clinical professionals.
* The **Consumer** dataset exposes a subset of all supported _Findings_ and _Conditions_, along with content that has been organized and tailored for non-clinical professionals.

Endpoints have been documented with separate requests for each of the Consumer and Clinical "_audiences_" in this API documentation. If your account grants access to both audiences, you may make requests to either endpoint freely.

#### Portability of data between Clinical and Consumer audiences

Because the Consumer audience uses a subset of the _Findings_ and _Conditions_ supported by the Clinical dataset, you may feasibly perform most operations across the boundary presented by the datasets. However there may be unintended consequences of doing this:

* Inference results computed using a Consumer dataset will not attempt to identify some lesions and conditions, which may cause the Clinical Differential endpoint to miss some potential _Conditions_.
* Submitting _Findings_ or _Conditions_ supported by the Clinical dataset to the Consumer Differential endpoint will result in a loss of these inputs.
* Attempting to retrieve information about Clinical _Findings_ or _Conditions_ from the Consumer Library Service endpoints will return _HTTP 404: Not Found_.
